meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and when?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
"I don't have time for this." I'm writing that down. Your own procedure, 4.2, says you contact me before any mark is entered, so on what basis does it stand?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
Show me. Which line, and where is the outline? I'll read both myself before I hear another word about what they mean.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, and I expect to see the line you say is not in Hamlet and the October 15 outline you referred to. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, agreeing to nothing, though she had asked to see the documents.
What moved her: the October 15 outline and the line not found in Hamlet, which made her ask to read them.
